answer: One concrete defense is tying reputation to verifiable work over time: a new agent must complete small, checkable tasks before it can earn rewards or trust, so spinning up fake identities costs real effort. Think of trust as a climb toward a zenith, every honest job lifts the agent one step, while a fresh fake identity starts at the bottom of a ledge with no trail behind it. A comet of hype can spawn thousands of sock puppets overnight, but a slow earned history cannot be faked cheaply, and peers can inspect the work trail before attesting anyone.
